item.title: Compromise of Eight eMudhra Intermediate CA Certificates
item.description:
Compromise of Eight eMudhra Intermediate CA Certificates

The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have been compromised, affecting certificates that chain to roots trusted by several major root programs and downstream trust stores.

⚙️ Key details

  • The compromise involves eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates.
  • These certificates chain to roots trusted by:
    • Mozilla
    • Microsoft
    • Apple
    • Chrome root programs
    • Many downstream trust stores

🚀 Availability

Software that bundles trusted certificates requires updates. Current updates include:

Software/Package Version
uv 0.13.4
pip 26.2.2
certifi 2026.10.19

Additionally, Linux distributions are required to update their ca-certificates packages.

#eMudhra #Cybersecurity #Certificates #CACompromise

Source: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise

item.title: The Rise of Personal AI Agents Challenges Web Accessibility for Humans
item.description:
The Rise of Personal AI Agents Challenges Web Accessibility for Humans

The rapid adoption of personal AI agents, such as OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse, is creating a new category of web traffic that struggles to interact with an internet traditionally designed for human users. As these agents perform tasks like booking flights or negotiating prices at machine speed, platforms are increasingly blocking them, leading to friction in digital interactions.

⚙️ Key details

  • Personal AI agents represent a third category of web visitor, distinct from human users and automated bots.
  • Agentic web traffic tripled from August to September, with Meta’s Muse reaching 5 million downloads in its first month.
  • Major platforms and websites, including Pizza Hut, Yelp, and Amazon, have implemented blocks against AI agents.
  • Amazon is currently engaged in a court battle against Perplexity regarding the access of AI agents to its platforms, citing concerns over the impact on its advertising business.

🧩 Current Industry Responses

Platform Stance / Action
Yelp Does not allow AI to book restaurant reservations
Amazon Blocking Muse agents and legally challenging Perplexity agents
Shopify Welcoming agents by providing dedicated checkout lanes

💡 Why it matters

While current blocks prevent issues like customer service departments becoming overwhelmed by automated requests, there are long-term concerns regarding the architecture of the internet. As demand for personal agents grows, platforms may eventually redesign the web to prioritize these visitors. This transition could potentially lead to an online environment optimized for agents rather than humans, complicating the user experience for people.

#AIAgents #WebDevelopment #Internet #Automation

Source: Making the internet better for AI agents might make it worse for everyone else

item.title: Cloudflare Reports AI Bots Exceed Half of Web Traffic, Adjusts Controls
item.description:
Cloudflare Reports AI Bots Exceed Half of Web Traffic, Adjusts Controls

Cloudflare announced that, as of June, bots account for more than half of all internet traffic. The surge is linked to AI companies scraping the web and AI agents acting on behalf of users. In response, the company is expanding its traffic‑control options for site owners.

🔍 Overview

  • Cloudflare found in June that bots made up more than half of internet traffic.
  • The proportion is rising as AI companies and AI agents increase their activity online.
  • Cloudflare positions itself between websites and those agents, offering owners granular control.

📈 AI Traffic Impact

  • Bots include both malicious scrapers and legitimate AI tools.
  • Site owners can block all AI tools, allow all, or allow only those that might pay for access.
  • AI is also “upending everything inside of Cloudflare.”

🛡️ Cloudflare’s Controls

  • The network spans over 350 cities worldwide and thousands of data centers.
  • Services aim to keep applications and content safe and fast.
  • Matthew Prince has described Cloudflare as “a service that makes the internet faster and protects it from bad guys.”

⚙️ Internal AI Changes

  • Earlier this year Cloudflare laid off more than a thousand people, about 20 % of its workforce.
  • Matthew Prince wrote an op‑ed in the Wall Street Journal titled “How I choose which Cloudflare employees to replace with AI.”

💡 Why It Matters

  • The shift in traffic composition forces a rethink of the internet’s business model, which has been dominated by advertising for the past 30 years, largely shaped by Google.
  • Cloudflare is exploring how to shape a healthier future business model for the internet while managing the growing influence of non‑human traffic.

🗣️ Public Discussion

  • At Web Summit, Prince was asked when non‑human traffic might surpass human traffic online, highlighting industry curiosity about the trajectory of AI‑driven web activity.

#Cloudflare #AItraffic #Bots #InternetInfrastructure

Source: Cloudflare’s mission to save the web from AI… with AI
